title: Impact of an Individualized Prehabilitation Program Combining Nutrition and Exercise on Skeletal Muscle Mass, Nutritional Status, and Quality of Life in Liver Transplant Candidates with Sarcopenia, Frailty, or Malnutrition
summary:
Patients with advanced liver disease frequently develop loss of muscle mass and strength, malnutrition, and reduced physical capacity. These changes can negatively affect quality of life and increase the risk of complications before and after liver transplantation. However, it remains unclear to what extent individually tailored nutritional and physical activity support before liver transplantation can be implemented in clinical practice and whether it can improve patients’ physical condition.

The aim of this study is to investigate the feasibility and acceptance of an individually tailored nutritional and physical activity intervention in adults on the waiting list for liver transplantation. In addition, the study will assess whether this intervention can improve muscle mass, nutritional status, physical performance, and quality of life, as well as help stabilize patients’ health status until transplantation. Outcomes after liver transplantation will be compared with anonymized data from comparable patients treated in previous years.
conditions: Diagnosis of liver cirrhosis (ICD-10-GM: K74.- and other etiology-specific ICD-10-GM codes) with approval for placement on the liver transplant waiting list.

interventions.name: Individualized preoperative nutrition and exercise prehabilitation for liver transplant candidates (regular individualized counseling via video consultations, quarterly assessment of sarcopenia, frailty, and nutritional status during the waiting period, and postoperative follow-up assessments until

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of advanced liver cirrhosis and approval for placement on the liver transplant waiting list by the Transplant Committee of the University Hospital Tübingen
- Presence of malnutrition, sarcopenia, or frailty
- Ability to provide written informed consent
- Willingness to participate in the lifestyle intervention
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute liver failure
- Diagnosed eating disorder
- Physical or cognitive limitations that preclude participation in the study intervention
